title: Isolation, culture, and immunophenotypic analysis of bone marrow HSPCs from patients with myelodysplastic syndromes
protocol: Dilute the BM sample 1:1 in DPBS in a 15 mL or 50 mL centrifuge tube, depending on the final sample volume.
Add the same volume of Ficoll medium into a clean centrifuge tube.
Load the diluted BM aspirate onto the Ficoll by tilting the tube at an angle of approximately 45°.
Load the pipette with the diluted BM aspirate.
Position the pipette tip at a 90° angle against the wall of the Ficoll-containing tube.
Slowly release the sample down the walls of the tube to form a layer on top of the Ficoll.
Remove the accelerator and brake functions of the centrifuge.
Spin down the tube(s) for 30 minutes at 685 × g and +18°C–22°C.
Carefully aspirate the upper phase (plasma) without perturbing the WBC ring.
In a clean centrifuge tube, add approximately twice the volume of washing buffer as the volume of diluted BM aspirate.
Collect the WBC ring by bringing the pipette tip to the surface and slowly aspirating in circular motion along the walls.
Transfer the cells into the tube containing the washing buffer.
Activate the accelerator and/or brake functions of the centrifuge.
Spin down for 10 minutes at 685 × g and +18°C–22°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Wash the sample by resuspending the pellet in 1 mL of washing buffer using a pipette to ensure there are no clumps.
If the sample was split into several tubes or if it was in a 50 mL tube, transfer each 1 mL cell suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube and bring their volume up to 10 mL with washing buffer.
Take a small aliquot of 20 μL and dilute it 1:1 with modified Turk’s solution for counting.
Mix briefly using the micropipette.
Add 2 volumes of DPBS or working solution to achieve a 1/4 dilution.
Count the nuclei in a hemocytometer.
Calculate the total number of MNCs in the sample based on the cell counts.
Take an aliquot containing 0.5–2 million cells for flow cytometry analysis and transfer it to a microcentrifuge tube.
Fixate the MNCs in the aliquot by adding a 1:1 volume of Streck™ cell preservative.
Store the aliquot according to the manufacturer’s specifications.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 475 × g and 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of washing solution.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 300 × g in a tabletop centrifuge at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant using a micropipette.
Resuspend the pellet in 300 μL of 1× MACS Rinsing solution.
Add 100 μL of FcR block to the sample.
Add 100 μL of anti-CD34 beads to the sample.
Mix by lightly pipetting up and down.
Incubate at 4°C for 30 min.
Prepare a magnetic column by placing it on the separator.
Condition the magnetic column by adding 3 ml of 1× MACS Rinsing solution and letting it elute into a tube or tray (discard).
Wash the cell suspension by adding 500 μL of Washing solution into the tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 300 × g and 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant using a micropipette.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of 1× MACS Rinsing solution for every 100 million cells.
Load the suspension into the column.
Place a 15 mL centrifuge tube under the column and on ice to collect the cell fraction enriched in CD34- cells.
Let the cell suspension go through the column entirely until the upper part is completely dry.
Add 2 mL of 1× MACS Rinsing solution to wash and let it elute entirely.
Repeat step b.
Place a clean 15 mL centrifuge tube containing 1 mL of Washing solution under the column and on ice.
Remove the column from the separator.
Add 5 mL of 1× MACS Rinsing solution to the column.
Use the provided plunger to apply gentle pressure to the column and quickly elute the cells that had been retained.
Add 5 mL of Washing buffer to the tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 475 × g and 4°C to pellet the cells.
Discard the supernatant by aspiration or decantation.
Remove any leftovers with a micropipette.
Resuspend the CD34+ pellet with 0.5–1 mL of pre-warmed HSPC Culture medium or Washing buffer for the CD34- fraction.
Transfer the cells to a microcentrifuge tube.
Take a 10 μL aliquot and combine it with Trypan blue (1:1).
Count the number of live cells.
Calculate the number of wells that can be plated and/or the final cell density per well.
Calculate the volume of cell suspension and fresh medium needed in each well (final volume = 0.5 mL/well in 48-well plates or 1 mL/well in 24-well plates).
Plan the number of cultured wells per sample, including controls relevant to the experiment.
Culture technical replicates; duplicates are sufficient but triplicates may be plated if enough cells are available.
Prioritize culturing the highest possible number of cells per well over having many wells per condition.
Plate single wells per condition when cell numbers are low and combine results with biological replicates during statistical analysis.
Prepare the culture plates using a micropipette to remove medium from MSC cultures without touching the bottom of the well.
Add 0.5–1 mL of pre-warmed DPBS to each well by placing the tip of the micropipette on the walls.
Swirl the plate and aspirate the DPBS with the micropipette to remove any dead cells left.
Add the corresponding volume of pre-warmed HSPC Culture medium calculated in step 27 to each well.
Split the cells into the wells as needed.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 2–16 h before treating them.
Note: De visu assessment of cellularity and viability under the microscope before treating the cells is recommended.
Add the corresponding drug and solvent solutions to each well.
Mix well by moving the plate horizontally in several directions in a cross-like pattern.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24–72 h (or up to 5 days) as needed before proceeding.
Prepare MNCs aliquoted after gradient separation for flow cytometry analysis.
Stain the MNCs aliquoted after gradient separation and the cultured CD34+ cell fraction for flow cytometry analysis of the immunophenotypic HSPC subpopulations.
Add counting beads to each of the cultured cell tubes as internal standards to normalize the number of cells recorded per sample.
Mix the contents of each well by pipetting up and down 2–3 times.
Transfer the cell suspensions to microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 250-500 μL of pre-warmed washing solution to each well.
Gently mix the washing solution with each well by pipetting up and down 2-3 times.
Transfer the content of each well to the corresponding tube, combining it with previously collected cell suspensions.
Centrifuge the tubes at 300 × g and 4°C for 10 min.
Collect a small aliquot (10%-20% v/v) of MNCs before proceeding if an unstained flow cytometry control is needed.
Centrifuge the collected aliquots along with the rest of the MNCs and CD34+ cells at 300 × g and 4°C for 10 min.
Keep the collected aliquots on ice until further processing.
Carefully aspirate the supernatants using a micropipette.
Add 100 μL of HSPC Staining cocktail to the MNCs sample, or 50 μL to each cultured sample, and mix briefly with the tip.
Incubate samples for 30–45 min at 4°C and protected from light.
Vortex OneComp eBeads thoroughly and aliquot 500 μL in a microcentrifuge tube.
Pipette 50 μL of beads into microcentrifuge tubes pre-labeled with the names of the 6 fluorochromes used in this panel.
Add 50 μL of Working solution to each tube, for a final volume of 100 μL.
Incubate for 15–30 min at 4°C and protected from light.
Prepare flow cytometry tubes for the cultured CD34+ samples by adding 5 μL of counting beads.
Thoroughly mix each tube using reverse pipetting.
If using strainer caps, remove the caps prior to adding the beads and then recap the tubes.
Keep tubes at 4°C and protected from light.
Add 100 μL of washing solution to each tube after incubation.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 300 × g and 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatants with a micropipette, leaving a marginal volume in CD34+ cell tubes.
Resuspend cell pellets, except for the unstained control, in 250–500 μL of SYTOX Green solution.
Resuspend CD34+ cells in 250–300 μL of SYTOX Green solution.
Resuspend MNCs in 350–500 μL of SYTOX Green solution.
Resuspend bead pellets and unstained control in 350–500 μL of Working solution.
Transfer corresponding suspensions into pre-labeled flow cytometry tubes.
Keep flow cytometry tubes at 4°C and protected from light until analysis.
Set the recording limit to 200,000–500,000 events for each sample.
Use total BM MNCs fixated in step 12 and stained in parallel with cultured samples to set up or adjust the flow cytometry template.
Record cultured samples entirely.
Set a low value for threshold or discriminator in the FSC channel to record counting beads.
Collect a minimum of 1,000 beads while recording each sample.
Select the cell population with low FSC and low SSC in a FSC vs. SSC plot.
Display the cells in a FSC-H vs. FSC-W plot and select the singlets.
Display the selected singlets in an FSC vs. FITC plot and select live cells: SYTOX Green- (FITC may be dim or negative).
Within live cells, select lineage-negative cells: SYTOX Green-, FITC-.
Display live Lin- cells in CD38-APC-Cy7 vs. CD34-BV421.
Select hematopoietic stem cells (CD34+, CD38-) and myeloid progenitor cells (CD34+, CD38+) from the displayed Lin- cells.
Display the CD34+, CD38- stem cell compartment in CD90-PerCP vs. CD45RA-APC.
Gate for Long term (LT)-HSCs: CD90+, CD45RA-.
Gate for Multipotent progenitors (MPPs): CD90-, CD45RA-.
Gate for Lymphoid-primed MPPs (LMPPs): CD90-, CD45RA+.
Display the CD34+, CD38+ myeloid progenitor compartment in CD45RA-APC vs. CD123-PE.
Gate for Common myeloid progenitors (CMPs): CD123+, CD45RA-.
Gate for Granulomonocytic progenitors (GMPs): CD123+, CD45RA+.
Gate for Megakaryocytic progenitors (MEPs): CD123-, CD45RA-.
Display the selected population in FSC vs. FITC.
Exclude scattered, FITC-high dead cell debris.
Gate two well-defined bead populations with low and medium-intensity FITC signals.
Create independent gates for A Beads and B Beads on FITC vs. PE display.
Calculate absolute number of cells using formula: Absolute cell count = (Number of cells in gate / Number of recorded beads) x Bead concentration (n/μL) x 5 μL.
Normalize data to the number of cells in the control sample.
